subject: Detection Function using G0 instead of Lambda when running HHN (Hazard Half Normal)

messages.author: 6f9aabe27bffadb7
messages.subject: Detection Function using G0 instead of Lambda when running HHN (Hazard Half Normal)
parts:
Hi Murray,

I am trying to fit a model using the HHN detection function on a multi session capthist file. 

Although I have specified which detection function to be used. I have noticed that the output is producing NA values for the Loglik and is not reflecting the use of Lambda as the parameter for the detection function.

I have included a screenshot of the output and an example of the multi session capthist file below. 

Any help on this would greatly be appreciated,
Lawrence

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Detection Function using G0 instead of Lambda when running HHN (Hazard Half Normal)
parts:
Hello Lawrence

I don't think this has anything (directly) to do with the choice of detection function. Your data are counts on a single occasion per session, with a 'usage' effort adjustment. For some reason that I have yet to pin down, secr.fit gags on this with other settings at their defaults. I can make it work by ignoring usage (details = list(ignoreusage = TRUE)) or by suppressing the 'fastproximity' default (details = list(fastproximity = FALSE)). The density and sigma estimates are virtually identical between these, only lambda0-hat differs (as expected: usage is in the range 0-1 and lambda0 per unit time/effort is increased). You do not gain from fastproximity when there is already a single occasion per session, so it is safe to switch it off (it is a bug that it was internally 'on' in this case).

Asides - I see you have all-negative detector coordinates; that is unusual but probably not a problem. The detection parameter is 'lambda0', which is unfortunately easy to confuse with other 'lambda's such as the finite rate of increase that appears as a parameter in its own right in secr 4.6.4 (via the Dlambda parameterisation).

Cheers
Murray

parts:
Hi Murray,

Thank you for getting back to me and for the in-depth response to this question.

I have given the fastproximity solution a go and it seems that it has solved the 'NA' Loglik issue I was experiencing. I still need to do a deeper analysis on these results, but this has been a great help so far and I genuinely appreciate your time on this.

I will also keep your observation about the detector coordinate projections in mind. This was based on the initial study, which used Albers Equal Area projections. I am open to suggestions if you believe there may be a better projection type to use here.

I hope you have a wonderful day further and thanks again,
Lawrence
